output.question: What lawsuits is DoorDash involved in?
output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, a prominent ongoing case is Uber’s lawsuit accusing DoorDash, Inc. of anticompetitive practices and interference with contracts; a November 9 appellate hearing concerned whether the dispute belongs in court or arbitration. DoorDash also faces Slawson v. DoorDash Inc., a Washington labor case in which it sought to compel arbitration on August 14, 2026, although I could not verify subsequent developments. More broadly, its quarterly report filed October 30, 2026 discloses Dasher independent-contractor classification litigation, consumer-protection and competition cases, data-protection claims, intellectual-property disputes, and accident-related personal-injury lawsuits. Separately, DoorDash announced a $131.5 million settlement of New York City delivery-worker pay enforcement proceedings on September 22, 2026—not an unresolved court lawsuit—and announced settlement of Chicago’s lawsuit over discontinued business practices on November 14, 2025.

key_facts.fact: As of November 9, 2026, Uber’s anticompetitive-practices and tortious-interference lawsuit against DoorDash was before a California appellate panel over whether arbitration should be required.
As of the docket’s August 14, 2026 update, Slawson v. DoorDash Inc. was a Washington federal labor case, and DoorDash had filed a motion to compel arbitration and stay proceedings.

DoorDash’s quarterly report for September 30, 2026, filed October 30, 2026, describes contractor-classification litigation and consumer, competition, data-protection, intellectual-property and personal-injury proceedings.
On September 22, 2026, DoorDash announced a $131.5 million settlement with New York City’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection over delivery-worker pay compliance.
On November 14, 2025, DoorDash announced that Chicago’s lawsuit over discontinued business practices had been settled without an admission of wrongdoing.

caveats: This is a selected overview, not an exhaustive inventory of every lawsuit involving DoorDash, Inc.
Allegations in pending lawsuits are not findings of liability.
The Slawson docket reviewed was last updated August 14, 2026; its current procedural status could not be verified.
The quarterly report groups many proceedings by subject rather than identifying every individual case.
The New York City pay matter is settled administrative enforcement, and the Chicago lawsuit is settled; neither should be presented as an unresolved court lawsuit.
